clue.text: Tips for safety connected with worry about second tree

indicators.note: the tips of a word are its two ends, so only the outermost letters are kept
one word goes round another, wrapping it on both sides

blocks.note: the first and last letters of safety
to worry is to care, as in cares of the world
a mo is a moment, a second

explanation.surface: Someone frets over a second tree while worrying about safety on the job.
explanation.walkthrough: Mo, short for moment, is the usual crossword second; it sits inside the worry word rather than after it.
explanation.definitionFit: The sycamore is a large maple species common in Britain and Europe, a familiar broadleaf variety.

clue.text: Smart agent inhibiting rest

indicators.note: to inhibit is to hold something in check, so the agent holds the other word inside

blocks.note: a secret agent is a spy
a nap is a short rest

explanation.surface: A sharp operative stops a colleague from taking a break.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Smart' reads as describing the agent, but it is the definition on its own.
explanation.definitionFit: A snappy dresser is stylishly turned out, so smart and snappy are synonyms describing neat appearance.

clue.text: Vote for champs vocally

indicators.note: said with the voice, so the word is judged by its sound rather than its spelling

blocks.note: to champ is to chew noisily, and chews sounds like the spelling given

explanation.surface: An election where you back the champions, cheered on loudly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Champs' looks like a noun for winners; here it is the verb champ, to chew.
explanation.definitionFit: Voting for a candidate is picking or selecting that person, the same act of making a choice.

clue.text: Feature with good system, being covered by damages for dismissal

indicators.note: something covered by another thing sits inside it, with the outer word on both sides

blocks.note: mars means spoils or damages
a facial feature
standard abbreviation for good
an order is a system or arrangement

explanation.surface: A legal note about compensation paid for sacking someone with a well-ordered process.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Damages' suggests legal compensation, but it is the verb meaning spoils.
explanation.definitionFit: Being given your marching orders is an idiom for being dismissed or told to leave a job.

clue.text: Odd unverified reports, not ours

indicators.note: 'not' tells us the following letters are taken out of the longer word

blocks.note: rumours are unconfirmed stories
taken as written, the letters to remove

explanation.surface: Strange gossip is going around, and it did not start with us.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing OURS from RUMOURS leaves RUM. Rum meaning odd is chiefly British.
explanation.definitionFit: In British usage rum is an informal adjective for strange or peculiar, as in a rum business.

clue.text: Exclude bishop for hurtful remark

blocks.note: to bar someone is to keep them out
chess notation abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: A cleric is banned from church for an insulting comment.
explanation.definitionFit: A barb is a cutting or wounding comment, named from the backward hook on an arrowhead.

clue.text: Old artist up above rival endlessly capturing one with fragrant quality

indicators.note: in a down clue, going up means reading the letters from bottom to top
without its end, so the final letter is dropped
to capture is to hold inside, so one piece is placed within the other

blocks.note: standard abbreviation for old
Royal Academician, a member of the Royal Academy of Arts
to match is to equal or rival
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: An elderly painter, ranked above a competitor, is caught out by a scent.
explanation.walkthrough: O + RA reads upwards as ARO; MATCH loses its H and takes in I, giving MAT(I)C. 'Above' places one part over the other in a down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Aromatic describes something giving off a pleasant, spicy smell, the property of having fragrance.

clue.text: Actor in hole after day gripped by horror

indicators.note: something gripped by another is held between its two sides

blocks.note: standard abbreviation for day
a pit is a hole in the ground
a little horror is a badly behaved child

explanation.surface: A performer stuck in a hole after a day of a horror film shoot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After day' fixes the order of the inner pair. Horror here means a naughty child, not the film genre.
explanation.definitionFit: Brad Pitt is an American film star, an example of the category of actor.

clue.text: Partisan, popular, challenged about religious education

indicators.note: one word goes round the other, surrounding it

blocks.note: in fashion, popular
put to the test, challenged
RE is the school subject Religious Education

explanation.surface: A biased, well-liked teacher was questioned over a religious studies lesson.
explanation.walkthrough: RE, Religious Education, is a standard subject in British schools.
explanation.definitionFit: An interested party has a stake in the outcome, so is not neutral but biased or one-sided.

clue.text: Changing topic at tea, list names for pieces of shortbread

indicators.note: changing the words means their letters are rearranged into a new order

blocks.note: the fourteen letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Switching subjects at teatime, someone lists what to call the shortbread.
explanation.definitionFit: Petticoat tails are triangular wedges of Scottish shortbread cut from a round, shaped like a hooped skirt's edge.

clue.text: Affair created by mail, for instance, right away

indicators.note: sent away means removed, so that letter disappears from the word

blocks.note: chain mail is an example of armour
standard abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A romance struck up through letters, with something proper gone missing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mail' suggests letters; it is the metal mesh worn as armour. Dropping its R leaves AMOUR.
explanation.definitionFit: An amour is a love affair, often a secret one, borrowed from the French word for love.

clue.text: State sources, including name, with love and thanks

indicators.note: including something means holding it within, so one letter goes inside

blocks.note: mines are sources of ore or riches
standard abbreviation for name
love is zero in tennis, the shape of O
ta is informal British for thanks

explanation.surface: A note citing named sources, signed off with love and gratitude.
explanation.definitionFit: Minnesota is one of the fifty US states, in the upper Midwest on the Canadian border.

clue.text: Situation? Summit's opening, amid enmity, without delay

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter
amid means in the middle of, so this letter sits inside the other word

blocks.note: a post is a job or position
first letter of summit
hate is strong enmity

explanation.surface: A diplomat's urgent question about the state of play as hostile talks begin.
explanation.definitionFit: Post-haste is an old adverb meaning with great speed, from the haste of the postal riders.

clue.text: Associations with strange days in sect

indicators.note: something strange is out of its normal form, so the letters are disordered

blocks.note: the ten letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Odd groups who spend peculiar days inside a religious cult.
explanation.definitionFit: Syndicates are groups of people or firms combining for a common business purpose, a kind of association.

clue.text: Walk miles in westward region

indicators.note: in an across clue, heading west means reading right to left
one letter is placed in the other word

blocks.note: a part of the country is a region
standard abbreviation for miles

explanation.surface: A hiker covers many miles heading west through a district.
explanation.definitionFit: To tramp is to walk a long way with heavy steps, as on a long trek or hike.

clue.text: Drama with end ruined by writing that's undistinguished

indicators.note: a ruined word has been wrecked, so its letters come out jumbled

blocks.note: No (or Noh) is classical Japanese drama
taken as written, to be rearranged
a script is handwriting or a written text

explanation.surface: A play whose ending was spoiled by poor writing is forgettable.
explanation.walkthrough: Drama gives NO, the Japanese theatre form, also spelt Noh.
explanation.definitionFit: Something nondescript lacks distinctive features and is hard to describe, so it is unremarkable or ordinary.

clue.text: Short of time, savour chance to be a star

indicators.note: short of means lacking, so that letter is removed

blocks.note: standard abbreviation for time
to savour is to taste with relish
to chance something is to risk it

explanation.surface: A hopeful performer, pressed for time, relishes the gamble of becoming famous.
explanation.walkthrough: TASTE loses its T to leave ASTE, then RISK follows. 'Star' suggests a celebrity; it is the printed symbol.
explanation.definitionFit: An asterisk is the small printed symbol shaped like a star, its name from the Greek for little star.

clue.text: Support stirring dinner up

indicators.note: stirring mixes things around, so the letters are mixed into a new order

blocks.note: the eight letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Someone helps out by stirring the evening meal in the kitchen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Up' looks like part of a phrasal verb 'stirring up' but belongs to the letters being rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: To underpin is to provide a foundation from below, so it means to support or prop up.

clue.text: Small orchestra's wavering tone is faint

indicators.note: something wavering is unsteady, so its letters shift into another order

blocks.note: the eleven letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A chamber ensemble plays with a wobbly, barely audible sound.
explanation.definitionFit: A sinfonietta is a chamber-sized ensemble, from the Italian diminutive of sinfonia, meaning a little symphony band.

clue.text: Fool with fantastic gossip

blocks.note: to con is to fool or trick
fab is short for fabulous, fantastic

explanation.surface: An idiot enjoys some brilliant tittle-tattle.
explanation.definitionFit: A confab, short for confabulation, is an informal chat or conversation, the sort of talk that passes news.

clue.text: Off course since attempt to skirt area

indicators.note: to skirt something here is to run around its edges, enclosing it

blocks.note: as in the sense of because
a try is an attempt
standard abbreviation for area

explanation.surface: A sailor wanders off course after trying to go round a region.
explanation.definitionFit: To go astray is to wander from the correct path or route, so it describes being lost.

clue.text: Revise measure in printing last section

blocks.note: an em is a printer's unit of width
the end is the final part

explanation.surface: An editor corrects the measurements in the final chapter of a print run.
explanation.definitionFit: To emend a text is to correct or improve it, which is what revising a draft does.

clue.text: Article university issues discounting English tests

indicators.note: discounting means leaving out of account, so that letter is dropped

blocks.note: the indefinite article
standard abbreviation for university
issues of a magazine are editions
standard abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: A college publishes papers but leaves out its English exams.
explanation.definitionFit: Auditions are trial performances by actors or musicians, tests of suitability for a role or place.

clue.text: Flawed rascal, free, in trouble with court

indicators.note: a word in trouble is in disarray, so its letters are thrown into another order

blocks.note: an imp is a mischievous child
taken as written, to be rearranged
standard abbreviation for court

explanation.surface: A scoundrel, out on bail, finds himself in trouble with the law again.
explanation.definitionFit: Something imperfect has faults or defects, so it is not complete or flawless.

clue.text: Number aboard slow train upset

indicators.note: aboard means riding inside, so the letters are carried within the words
upset means turned over, so the letters run the other way up the column

blocks.note: the letters straddle the gap between the pair of words

explanation.surface: A number of passengers on a delayed train are annoyed.
explanation.definitionFit: Two is a whole counting value, the integer after one, so it is a numeral.

clue.text: Deduce sign of fear, odd characters having fled

indicators.note: once the odd-numbered letters have run away, only the even ones remain

blocks.note: the second, fourth, sixth, eighth and tenth letters

explanation.surface: A detective spots someone trembling as strange figures run off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Odd characters' reads like suspicious people; it means the odd-numbered letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To infer is to reach a conclusion by reasoning from evidence, which is what deducing means.

clue.text: Helpful style

blocks.note: first meaning: considerate and generous
second meaning: a sort or type

explanation.walkthrough: One word, two senses: the adjective for good-natured and the noun for a category.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes someone friendly and obliging; the noun means a sort, type or manner of thing.

clue.text: Excited by spoils, perhaps

indicators.note: excited things are agitated and moving about, so the letters are stirred up

blocks.note: the eight letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Someone might be thrilled by the loot from a raid, maybe.
explanation.definitionFit: Possibly and perhaps are adverbs of uncertainty, both meaning that something may be so.
